body: The `key={key}` prop was dropped when `GrafanaRuleLoader` was replaced with `GrafanaRuleListItem`. This element is returned from inside a `.map()`, so React now warns about missing keys and falls back to reconciling by index. As filter results stream in or reorder, list items (and state such as an open menu or modal) can be attached to the wrong rule. Please restore `key={key}`.

The list view no longer fetches ruler rules, so `rulerRule` is undefined there. That means the new `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` result for Pause is effectively ignored: this branch still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, so "Pause/Resume evaluation" never appears in the new list view. It was available before, when `GrafanaRuleLoader` fetched the ruler rule. `MenuItemPauseRule` needs a way to work from the prom rule (for example, lazily fetching the ruler rule on click).

Same regression for Delete: `canDelete` can now be true from the prom-rule abilities, but the item is still gated on `rulerRule` being defined. In the list view (prom rule only) the Delete action is silently hidden for users who have permission to delete, which removes a capability the list had before this PR.

The silence drawer only renders when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true. In the list view only `promRule` is passed, so `rule` is undefined. The menu still shows "Silence notifications", because `canSilence` is now computed from the prom rule, but clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer` and nothing opens. Either make `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` accept the prom rule (it mainly needs the uid) or hide the menu item when no ruler rule is available.

Behaviour differs from `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`: that hook gates Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently and ModifyExport on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for Grafana recording rules as well as alerting rules. Here they are gated on `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, so Grafana-managed recording rules lose Pause, Export and Restore in the list view even though they support them. Use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` for these (keep the alerting-only check for Silence).

Changing `=== null` to `== null` makes this loop unbounded. It never checks `leftIdx < yData.length`, and reading past the end of the array returns `undefined`, which now satisfies `== null`. Previously `undefined === null` was false, so the loop stopped at the end of the array. If a series is entirely null or undefined when this path runs, the loop never terminates and the browser tab freezes. Add `leftIdx < yData.length` to the condition.

`useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns `isEditable: false` whenever the folder cannot be loaded, including while `useFolder` is still loading. Combined with `MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`, every list row first renders without Edit, Pause or Delete and they only appear once the folder resolves. It also issues one folder request per rule on the list page (N rows mean N `useFolder` calls, unless they are deduplicated by cache). Please confirm this is deduped and acceptable for large lists.

The ruler/prom matching was removed along with the `Creating` and `Deleting` operation rows. Rules that were just created (present in the ruler but not yet in prom) or just deleted (still in prom) are no longer shown with a pending state. A just-deleted rule now appears as a normal, actionable row, and actions on it will fail. If this is intentional because prom is now strongly consistent, the `operation` prop on `GrafanaRuleListItem` is dead code and should be removed.
